title: Logging a set from the notification or the watch with the app closed is only checked by reading the code as text
what: When the app is closed, the phone itself ticks the set, starts the rest, moves the card on and keeps the tick for the app. The only test for this phone part opens the code files and looks for certain lines in them. It never runs the logic, so a wrong set picked, a tick kept twice, a stale card acted on, or a rest started at the wrong length would all still pass.
expected: A test that really runs the phone part with a saved plan and checks which set is kept, that a second tap is ignored, that an old card is left for the app, and that the rest starts with the right length.
who: members who log sets from the notification or a watch
how_often: every release that touches this part
fix_line: Add a native test that runs the closed-app tick with a saved plan and checks the result

title: Most of the phone's own native parts have no test at all, and some phone tests never run before a release
what: Only five native test files exist in this area: the alert ring, the watch messages, the workout clock and the gym shortcut picture. The rest card, the live workout card, start-up recovery, the home-screen widgets, Health Connect, in-app update and the Google Play payment part have none. The release run checks only the rest and watch tests; the gym shortcut tests run only when those exact files change. On the app side, the Health Connect, Reminders and Widgets settings cards and the widget's one-time start key are not used by any test.
expected: Every native part that keeps a promise to the member (rest alerts, widgets, Health Connect, payments) has at least one real test, and all native tests run before every release.
how_often: every release that changes these parts
fix_line: Add tests for the rest card, widgets, Health Connect and payment parts, and run all native tests in the release run

title: Sets logged with the app closed are quietly thrown away if their saved list cannot be read
what: Sets ticked from the notification or the watch while the app is closed wait in a saved list. If that list ever cannot be read back, the next tap starts a fresh empty list and saves it over the old one, so the earlier sets are lost. Nothing is written to the log when this happens.
expected: A list that cannot be read is kept aside and reported in the log, never silently replaced.
who: members who log sets from the notification or a watch
how_often: very rare, only if the saved list is damaged
fix_line: Log a warning and keep the damaged list instead of overwriting it

items.reason: no flaky-run record exists in the machine files; the native tests use no sleeps, clocks or network, and the phone unit tests in this area fix the time where they use it; one Health Connect test waits two event-loop turns, which is fragile but steady
